passages.title: Beans and Music
passages.passage: Every March our school holds a science fair in the sports hall, and this year I finally decided to take part (1)____ it. My partner, Minh, and I wanted to find out (2)____ or not plants grow faster when they listen to music, so we set up three pots of beans on the windowsill of his bedroom. One pot heard pop songs every evening, one heard classical music, and the third was left in silence. For four weeks we measured the plants every morning (3)____ we could compare them fairly. To be honest, the beans did not seem to care about the music at all, (4)____ we were a little disappointed. However, our teacher said that a result which surprises you is still a result. On the day of the fair, we (5)____ a large poster with our graphs and a photo of each pot. Dozens of parents and younger students walked past our table, and some of them stopped to ask questions. One little boy wanted to know if the beans liked pop or classical music, and Minh had to explain that they liked (6)____. In the afternoon, three judges, each of (7)____ carried a clipboard, came to look at every project. They were impressed by (8)____ carefully we had recorded our data, even though our idea was quite simple. We did not win first prize, (9)____ went to a girl who built a small water filter out of sand and charcoal. All the same, we got a certificate, and we have already decided (10)____ something with electricity next year.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is take part in an event. On, at and of never follow take part.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Only whether can be followed directly by or not. If also introduces an indirect question, but if or not is not possible; that and what do not report a yes/no question.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: So that + could expresses purpose: they measured every morning in order to compare the plants. Because would give a reason, not a purpose, and although and unless make no sense here.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The disappointment is the result of the beans ignoring the music, and a result is introduced by so. But and although would signal a contrast; because would reverse cause and effect.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: You put up a poster, meaning you fix it on a wall or board. Put off means postpone, put out means extinguish, and put on is for clothes or a show.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Two kinds of music were mentioned, and the beans liked not one and not the other, so neither is the answer. None is for three or more, either would need a negative verb, and both is the opposite meaning.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: After a preposition the relative pronoun for people is whom: each of whom. Who cannot follow of in this structure, which is for things, and them would create two main clauses joined by nothing.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: How + adverb (how carefully) introduces the clause that the judges admired. That and which cannot go with carefully, and what carefully is not English.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A non-defining relative clause after a comma needs which to refer back to first prize. That is not used after a comma, who is for people, and what does not refer back to a noun.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The verb decide is followed by a to-infinitive: decided to try. It never takes an -ing form or a bare verb.

passages.title: Ninety Kilometres to the Sea
passages.passage: Last summer my cousin Huy and I cycled from our town to the coast, a distance of almost ninety kilometres. We had been planning the trip (1)____ the beginning of the year, but our parents only agreed after we promised to phone them every two hours. We set (2)____ at six in the morning, when the roads were still empty and the air was cool. For the first hour everything went smoothly, and we felt (3)____ proud of ourselves that we started singing. Then, just outside a village, Huy's back tyre went flat. Neither of us had ever repaired a tyre before, (4)____ luckily we had a small kit in Huy's bag. A farmer who was passing by on his motorbike stopped and showed us (5)____ to do, and twenty minutes later we were back on the road. By midday the sun was so hot that we (6)____ to rest under a tree and drink nearly all our water. I have to admit that I was tempted to give (7)____ and catch a bus, but Huy refused to listen. In the afternoon the land became flatter and we could smell the sea long before we saw it. We finally reached the beach at half past four, (8)____ tired than we had expected but extremely happy. My aunt, (9)____ house is near the harbour, had prepared a huge dinner for us. Looking back, I think the journey taught me more about patience than any lesson at school (10)____ has.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The past perfect continuous with a starting point takes since: had been planning since the beginning of the year. For needs a length of time, and from and during do not combine with this tense in this way.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Set off means to begin a journey. Set up means to establish, set down means to put something down, and set in is used for weather or a season.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Before an adjective, the result structure is so + adjective + that. Such needs a noun, and too and very cannot be followed by a that-clause of result.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The second half contrasts with the first: they had no experience, but they did have a kit. So and because would link cause and result, and unless makes no sense.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Do needs an object, and what supplies it: showed us what to do. How to do would need it after it, and which and that cannot stand alone here.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Only had can be followed by to: had to rest expresses necessity in the past. Must, should and could take a bare infinitive, never to.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Give up means to stop trying. Give off is for smells or heat, give away means to donate, and give out means to distribute.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The comparative before than is more tired. Most is a superlative, and much and very cannot be followed by than without a comparative.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The house belongs to the aunt, so the possessive relative whose is needed before the noun house. Who, which and that cannot show possession.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: After a comparison with than any, ever means at any time. Never would make the sentence illogical, and always and yet do not fit this structure.

passages.title: Eighty Candles in the Garden
passages.passage: My grandmother turned eighty last month, and my family decided to throw her a surprise party. This was far (1)____ easy than it sounds, because she is the kind of person who notices everything. My mother told her that we were all going out for a quiet lunch, (2)____ she believed without asking a single question. The hardest part was keeping the secret (3)____ my little brother, who cannot stay quiet for more than five minutes. In the end we simply did not tell him until the morning of the party. I was (4)____ charge of the cake, which I had ordered from a bakery near my school. Unfortunately, when I went to collect it, the shop was closed, and I had to wait outside for nearly an hour (5)____ the owner arrived. (6)____, my cousins were hanging lanterns in the trees and my father was laying the tables in the garden. At exactly twelve o'clock my mother drove Grandma through the gate. When everybody jumped out and shouted, she was so shocked that she dropped her handbag. Then she started laughing and could not stop. She told us later that she (7)____ suspected something the week before, when my aunt asked her about her favourite songs, but she had decided to say nothing. We spent the whole afternoon eating, singing and looking (8)____ old photographs. My grandfather, who passed away three years ago, would have loved every minute of it. Before we left, Grandma made (9)____ promise to do the same thing for her ninetieth birthday. I do not think (10)____ of us would dare to refuse.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The comparative before than is less easy. Fewer goes with plural nouns, least is a superlative, and little is not a comparative form.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: After a comma, the relative pronoun that refers to the whole idea of the previous clause is which. That cannot start a non-defining clause, who is for people, and what does not refer back.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: You keep a secret from somebody, meaning you do not let that person know. Of, to and off do not form this collocation.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The expression is in charge of something, meaning responsible for it. The other prepositions never combine with charge in this sense.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The waiting continued up to the moment the owner arrived, which is expressed by until + clause. While would describe two actions happening together, and during and by are prepositions that cannot introduce a clause here.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Meanwhile links two things happening at the same time: the narrator was waiting while the family prepared the garden. However needs a contrast, therefore a result, and otherwise a condition.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The suspicion came before the moment of telling, so the past perfect had suspected is needed. Has is present perfect, and was and would cannot combine with suspected in this meaning.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Viewing photographs is looking at them. Look for means search, look after means take care of, and look up means find information.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The structure is make somebody promise, so the object pronoun us is needed. We is a subject pronoun, and our and ours are possessives.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: After a negative verb (do not think), the quantifier is any: I do not think any of us. Some is for positive sentences, none would create a double negative, and every cannot be followed by of us.

passages.title: The Peacock and the Sandwich
passages.passage: When I was nine, my class went on a day trip to the city zoo, and I still remember it more clearly (1)____ any other trip from primary school. We arrived so early (2)____ the gates had only just opened and the paths were almost empty. Our teacher divided us (3)____ groups of five and gave each group a map and a list of animals to find. My group headed straight for the elephants, (4)____ we could hear long before we could see them. One of them was spraying water over its back with its trunk, and a baby elephant was trying to copy it (5)____ much success. After that we spent nearly half an hour watching the monkeys, which seemed just as interested (6)____ us as we were in them. The keeper told us that the oldest monkey had lived at the zoo (7)____ more than thirty years. At lunchtime we sat on the grass near the lake, and a peacock walked up to us and stole a piece of bread (8)____ of my friend's hand. Everyone laughed except my friend, who had been waiting for that sandwich all morning. In the afternoon it began to rain, so we sheltered in the reptile house, where I saw a snake for the first time in my life. I was not brave (9)____ to touch it, although the keeper said it was completely harmless. On the bus home, our teacher asked us to write a few sentences about our favourite animal. I chose the baby elephant, and I wrote that if I ever became a zookeeper, I (10)____ look after the elephants and nothing else.

questions.q: Blank (1): write one word.
questions.explanation: The comparative more clearly must be completed with than. As is used only with as ... as, not after more.

questions.q: Blank (2): write one word.
questions.explanation: So early sets up a result clause, and a result clause begins with that. When or because would break the so ... that structure.

questions.q: Blank (3): write one word.
questions.explanation: The verb divide takes into before the parts that are formed: divided us into groups. In does not show the change from one whole to several parts.

questions.q: Blank (4): write one word.
questions.explanation: A non-defining relative clause after a comma referring to the elephants needs which. That is not used after a comma, and who is reserved for people.

questions.q: Blank (5): write one word.
questions.explanation: The baby elephant was trying and failing, so it copied its mother without much success. With would mean the opposite, and much after with would need a negative verb earlier.

questions.q: Blank (6): write one word.
questions.explanation: The adjective interested is always followed by in, and the sentence repeats the same preposition later (in them). About or on never follow interested.

questions.q: Blank (7): write one word.
questions.explanation: More than thirty years is a length of time, so it takes for. Since would need a starting point such as a year or a date.

questions.q: Blank (8): write one word.
questions.explanation: The phrase is out of somebody's hand, showing movement from inside to outside. From cannot be followed by of, and off would describe a surface, not a hand holding something.

questions.q: Blank (9): write one word.
questions.explanation: After an adjective, the degree word that takes a to-infinitive is enough: brave enough to touch. Too comes before the adjective and gives the opposite meaning.

questions.q: Blank (10): write one word.
questions.explanation: The if-clause uses the past simple (became), so this is a second conditional and the main clause needs would (or could / might). Will belongs to the first conditional and cannot follow an unreal past-tense condition.
